keyFindings.description: Documentation correctness: the passage ends '`ignoreMutation` is always true, since the swap from `` to `` is the one DOM change it makes itself and is never an edit' - the view has had no `ignoreMutation` since 8af418cf (picture-view.ts returns `{ dom }` or `{ dom, stopEvent }`), removed because `() => true` swallowed ProseMirror's selection record (round 1). The sentence documents the round-1 defect as a rule a future reader would restore. Correct statement: the view sets no `ignoreMutation`; prosemirror-view's leaf default (`!contentDOM && mutation.type != "selection"`, dist/index.js:1110-1111) already ignores the swap and still reports selection records.

Documentation correctness: 'the read-only version view has no click handler so there the browser follows its `href`' is not what happens. `click` is not a prosemirror-view native handler, so proof-editor's `markdownLinkClickPlugin` (`handleDOMEvents.click`, lib.ts:343) runs ungated by `stopEvent`; on a non-editable view `shouldOpenLinkForEvent` is `!event.defaultPrevented` and the plugin `preventDefault`s and opens the href in a new tab (`window.open(href, '_blank', 'noopener,noreferrer')`) - the tester observed exactly this. In the live editor the in-app navigation also depends on that plugin declining an unmodified primary click on an editable view (markdown-link-click.ts:521-527). Same passage: `RefPreviewHost` is not the only hover card - the library's link card (`handleMouseMove` -> `showCardForLink`, any `a[href]` outside `[data-mark-id]`, editable view) opens on the same element, so a fallback link shows two cards; settle (suppress one) or document.
The exhaustive list of specs the `firefox` Playwright project runs was not extended with `e2e/picture-link-click.e2e.ts`, which playwright.config.ts:151-152 now matches.

Hardening: `stopEvent` is still true for `dragstart` whose target is inside the link. `link.draggable = false` removes the known path (the wrapper is the drag source), but a drag of a DOM selection made over the link's words still fires `dragstart` inside the link, leaves `view.dragging` null and sends the drop down `handleDrop`'s external-HTML branch - the round-1 shape. Returning false for `dragstart` costs nothing: `handlers.dragstart` (:3816-3819) resolves the wrapper's desc and drags the picture node. Not reproduced in a browser.

Structure (Fast-follow): the Firefox caret workaround's reason lives in picture-view.ts:31-40 and its implementation (the `TextSelection` dispatch at `getPos() + node.nodeSize`) in ask-block.ts; a `pictureNodeView(view)` exported from picture-view.ts would keep them together and leave ask-block.ts to the typed blocks.
